property_summary: For any valid interfaceId, supportsInterface should return true if it matches the supported interfaces; the mutant always returns false, so there exists an interfaceId where the correct contract returns true and the mutant returns false.

For any given bytes4 interfaceId, the reference C's supportsInterface should return true if and only if the interfaceId matches IAccessControl or IERC165; the mutant always returns false, so for any interfaceId matching these, the reference returns true while the mutant returns false.
For the IERC165 interface ID (0x01ffc9a7) the reference returns true and the mutant returns false.

For any interfaceId, the reference C's supportsInterface returns true iff interfaceId matches IAccessControl or IERC165; the mutant always returns false, so for the IAccessControl interface ID the reference returns true while the mutant returns false.

For any preimage, if supportsInterface returns true once, it must return true again when called with the same interfaceId; the reference preserves idempotence (no side-effects on success), but the mutant returns false for all inputs, breaking idempotence for interface IDs that formerly returned true.
supportsInterface must return false for an interfaceId that is not IAccessControl or IERC165; the mutant returns true for any interfaceId, breaking the spec.
For any interfaceId that is not type(IAccessControl).interfaceId and not type(IERC165).interfaceId, supportsInterface must return false; the mutant returns true for all interfaceIds.

For any interfaceId that is not type(IERC165).interfaceId and not type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, the reference contract's supportsInterface must return false, while the mutant returns true for all inputs.
supportsInterface must return true for exactly both type(IERC165) and type(IAccessControl) interface IDs; the bug returns false for type(IAccessControl).
supportsInterface must return true for any registered interface ID supported by AccessControl (including IAccessControl) plus IERC165; the bug returns false for type(IAccessControl).

Reference C's supportsInterface must return true for the IAccessControl interface ID because it overrides to check it; the mutant returns false because it only calls super (ERC165) which does not recognize IAccessControl.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true if and only if the interfaceId has been registered as supported; the bug omits IAccessControl, so it returns false for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId while the reference returns true.

supportsInterface must return true exactly for the interface IDs the contract actually supports (IERC165 and IAccessControl); the mutant removes IAccessControl support, so it returns false for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId.

For all interfaceId inputs, supportsInterface must return true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId (0x7965db0b); the original contract always returns true while the mutant incorrectly returns false for this specific interfaceId.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true if and only if interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId; the mutant incorrectly returns false for that interfaceId and true for type(IERC165).interfaceId, breaking correspondence.

For any valid bytes4 interfaceId, the correct contract C returns true when interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId; the mutant instead returns true when interfaceId equals type(IERC165).interfaceId and false for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, violating the expected interface support mapping.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must always return true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId; the mutant replaces this check with type(IERC165).interfaceId, returning false for the IAccessControl identifier.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for either type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId, but never true for both; the mutant returns true for the same interfaceId as the original for type(IERC165).interfaceId, but false for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, while the original returns true for that one.

For any role and any account, c.hasRole(role, account) must return true if and only if the role was previously granted to the account; the bug always returns false, violating the rule for any granted role-account pair.

For any role not granted to any account, hasRole must return false; the bug also returns false, but the reference returns true when the role was previously granted, violating the invariant that hasRole only returns true if the role was granted.
For any role and any account, an account that has been granted the role via _setupRole must have hasRole return true; the bug breaks this by returning false for granted roles.

For any role not granted to an account, hasRole must return false, but if the role was then granted and not later revoked, hasRole must return true; the bug permanently returns false after granting, violating the second case.

For any role and account, the result of hasRole(role, account) must equal the stored membership of that role for that account in the contract; the bug always returns false regardless of the stored membership.

For any role and account, the result of hasRole(role, account) must equal the actual membership in the role's members mapping, but the mutant always returns true, breaking when the account is not a member.
For any role and account, renouncing the role by `account` must cause `hasRole(role, account)` to return false, but the mutant always returns true after renunciation.

For any role and account, hasRole must return the same boolean as the internal membership mapping _roles[role].members[account]; the bug by negating the return value breaks this equality for any non-zero membership state.

For any role and account, hasRole must return true when the account has been granted the role through _setupRole; the bug inverts this so an account that just received a role is reported as not having it.

For any role and account, `hasRole(role, account)` must return the same boolean as whether `account` is a member of `role` as reflected by a subsequent role-granting operation; the bug negates the return value, so granting a role and then calling `hasRole` returns `false` instead of `true`.

For any role and account, calling hasRole must return the same value as checking the membership directly for a role that was setup in the constructor; the bug negates the return value, so an account that was granted a role during construction returns false where the correct contract returns true.

For any role, the admin role returned by getRoleAdmin must be the one previously set via _setRoleAdmin; the mutant breaks this by always returning zero, so a non-zero admin role set in construction will differ.

For any role, the admin role returned by getRoleAdmin must equal the admin role stored by a preceding _setRoleAdmin call; the mutant always returns zero, violating this for any role whose stored admin role is non-zero.

For any role that was granted to an account via grantRole, the admin role returned by getRoleAdmin for that role must equal the admin role of the caller that successfully performed the grant, but the mutant always returns zero instead of the stored admin role.

The admin role of any role that has been set as its own admin (self-administered) via _setRoleAdmin must equal that role itself; the mutant returns zero for every role, breaking this for self-administered roles.
For any role, getRoleAdmin must return the admin role stored in the contract; the mutant always returns zero, violating this for any role that has a non-zero admin role.
